The bill would create a new statutory agency called the Office for Regional Australia.
The Office would hold inquiries, coordinate policy, support regional development committees, and advise the minister on regional deals and planning.
The minister must table a statement of the government's regional policy at least once every five years, and the Office must deliver a 'Regional Australia Impacts Report' by 1 October each year.
Establishes the Office for Regional Australia as a statutory agency.
Gives the Office powers to conduct inquiries and research, similar to the Productivity Commission.
Requires the Office to support the Regional Development Australia committee network with policy and research.
Requires the Office to provide advice to the minister on regional deals and evaluate existing deals.
Requires the minister to table a regional policy statement at least every five years.
Provides for the appointment of a parliamentary joint committee to oversee the Office.
People and communities in regional Australia, government bodies, the Regional Development Australia committee network, and the minister.

The Office for Regional Australia Bill 2019 was moved for a second reading, arguing the government's response to the *Regions at the ready* report was inadequate and calling for a permanent office modelled on the Productivity Commission to develop long-term regional policy. The bill would create an office to support regional planning, hold inquiries, and establish a parliamentary joint committee on regional development.
